hero.headline: Russell Wilson retires from NFL at 37, joins CBS Sports
hero.body:
Russell Wilson announced his retirement from professional football at age 37, ending a 13-year NFL career that included a Super Bowl championship and ten Pro Bowl selections. The veteran quarterback will transition to a broadcasting role with CBS Sports.

Wilson led the Seattle Seahawks to their first Super Bowl victory in 2014, defeating the Denver Broncos. Over his career, he established himself as one of the most successful quarterbacks of his generation, earning Pro Bowl honors ten times. His playing career included stints with the Seahawks, Broncos, and most recently another team before his retirement announcement.

The quarterback posted a video message titled "thank you, football" as he confirmed the career change to broadcasting. CBS Sports will add Wilson to its NFL coverage team, though specific details about his role have not been disclosed. The network gains a recently retired player with extensive playoff experience and deep knowledge of the modern game.

Wilson's retirement creates an immediate impact for his most recent team. Aaron Glenn, speaking about the quarterback situation, acknowledged Wilson's new television position and indicated his organization is evaluating options at the quarterback position. The timing of Wilson's announcement, coming during the offseason, allows teams to adjust their rosters and draft strategies accordingly.

The move from playing to broadcasting represents a growing trend of recently retired NFL players moving directly into media roles. Wilson's decade-plus of starting experience and championship pedigree position him as a potentially valuable analyst for CBS's NFL programming. His retirement removes one of the league's most recognizable veteran quarterbacks from active competition.

cards.headline: Trump to nominate Todd Blanche as attorney general
cards.teaser: President Trump announced he will formally nominate acting Attorney General Todd Blanche to lead the Justice Department.
cards.body:
President Trump will formally nominate acting Attorney General Todd Blanche to serve as the nation's top prosecutor. Trump announced the decision Wednesday evening, with nomination paperwork expected Thursday. Blanche previously worked as Trump's personal criminal defense attorney before being appointed to lead the Justice Department in an acting capacity.

If confirmed by the Senate, Blanche would become the administration's permanent attorney general. The Senate confirmation process will allow lawmakers to examine his record and qualifications for the role.

cards.headline: Trump picks Bill Pulte to lead intelligence community
cards.teaser: The president tapped the current head of the Federal Housing Finance Agency to additionally serve as acting director of national intelligence.
cards.body:
President Trump announced Bill Pulte, who currently leads the Federal Housing Finance Agency, will serve as acting director of national intelligence without seeking Senate confirmation. The move has drawn criticism from lawmakers, including Republican Mitch McConnell, who suggested Pulte is unfit for the role.

The appointment is complicating efforts to renew warrantless surveillance powers in Congress. Lawmakers are expressing hesitation about extending these authorities given Trump's approach to filling senior intelligence positions without legislative approval, potentially jeopardizing the renewal process.

cards.headline: Israel Strikes Hezbollah Targets Hours After New Lebanon Cease-Fire Begins
cards.body:
Israel launched intensified military operations against Hezbollah positions shortly after a new cease-fire agreement with Lebanon took effect, according to Israeli officials and reports from the region. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered the escalation, stating he had instructed the military to "crush" Hezbollah through expanded offensive operations.

The U.S.-brokered cease-fire agreement, announced following negotiations in Washington, required a complete cessation of fire from Hezbollah and the evacuation of its fighters south of the Litani River in southern Lebanon. However, the truce quickly fractured as both sides resumed military operations within hours of the announcement.

Hezbollah responded to what it characterized as Israeli violations of the cease-fire by launching several attacks on Monday. The Iranian-backed group claimed responsibility for at least four drone strikes on Shomera barracks in northern Israel, attacks on two additional military barracks in the region, and another strike on a military post in Misgav Am. These operations occurred at short intervals throughout the day.

Netanyahu justified the military escalation in a video statement posted on his messaging channel. "I have ordered an even greater acceleration of our operations," he said. "It is true that they are attacking us with drones, including fiber-optic drones, but we have teams working on countermeasures and we will solve this issue. We will intensify our blows, increase our firepower, and we will crush them."

The Israeli air force conducted successive strikes across southern Lebanon and the Bekaa Valley in eastern Lebanon on Monday evening. According to Lebanon's National News Agency, these operations killed three people and prompted evacuation orders for ten villages. Israel accused Hezbollah of breaching the truce agreement, citing continued drone attacks across the border.

The escalation reflects deep skepticism about the cease-fire's viability. The original negotiations that produced the agreement did not include direct participation from Hezbollah, raising questions about whether the group would honor terms to which it was not party. The military force has operated with significant autonomy within Lebanon, maintaining capabilities separate from the Lebanese government.

According to Lebanese authorities, Israeli strikes since early March have killed more than 3,100 people. The Israeli military reported that one soldier was killed on Sunday in southern Lebanon, bringing the total number of Israeli military deaths to 23 since hostilities erupted on March 2. One civilian contractor has also been killed.

Two far-right Israeli ministers called for further expansion of military operations. Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich and National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir separately urged intensified warfare and territorial control expansion.

The conflict between Israel and Hezbollah has persisted since March 2, with the April 17 cease-fire proving ineffective at stopping near-daily exchanges of fire between the two sides.

cards.headline: Ireland Plans Military Expansion Amid European Security Concerns
cards.teaser: The traditionally neutral country is working to address gaps in its defense capabilities.
cards.body:
Ireland is moving to strengthen its military forces as European nations reassess their security posture in light of perceived threats from Russia. The Irish government acknowledged it is working to address deficiencies in its armed forces, which have long reflected the country's tradition of neutrality.

Irish officials have described their country as a weak link in European defense infrastructure. The planned expansion represents a

cards.headline: Four House Republicans vote against Trump on Iran resolution
cards.teaser: A House resolution on Iran revealed growing impatience with Trump's military policy, even within his own party.
cards.body:
The House of Representatives delivered a significant rebuke to President Trump on Wednesday by voting 215 to 208 in favor of a war powers resolution that would force him to seek congressional approval before continuing military operations against Iran or withdraw U.S. forces from the conflict.

Four Republicans joined all Democrats to support the measure. The dissident Republicans were Thomas Massie of Kentucky, Brian Fitzpatrick of Pennsylvania, Warren Davidson of Ohio, and Tom Barrett of Michigan.

The vote represents a notable moment of Republican defection on a key foreign policy issue. It demonstrates that some members of Trump's own party are willing to challenge his approach to military conflict, despite the president's significant influence over the GOP.

The resolution now moves to the Senate, where lawmakers must promptly take up the measure under the war powers law. A handful of Senate Republicans previously joined Democrats in advancing a similar resolution last month, indicating potential support in the upper chamber as well.

This marks the fourth time the House has voted on a resolution designed to limit Trump's authority to continue the Iran conflict, which has now lasted more than 90 days. House Republicans had previously cancelled an earlier scheduled vote, recognizing they lacked sufficient numbers to block the measure's passage.

The timing of the vote comes as diplomatic efforts to negotiate a settlement have stalled. Trump administration officials have repeatedly claimed that a deal is close and that Iran is eager to reach an agreement, but concrete progress remains elusive.

The war powers resolution is largely symbolic in nature, as significant procedural hurdles remain before Congress could actually compel the president to end military operations. The measure would require Senate passage and potentially a presidential veto override to become binding policy. Still, the House vote signals growing frustration among lawmakers across the aisle regarding the administration's handling of the conflict.

The four Republican defectors represent a minority within their party, but their willingness to break ranks highlights the genuine concerns some GOP members hold about executive power in military matters. Historically, questions about the balance between presidential authority and congressional oversight in military conflicts have periodically united lawmakers across party lines.

The vote reflects evolving dynamics within Congress as members grapple with the ongoing tension between supporting a president of their own party and asserting institutional congressional powers over matters of war and peace. The resolution's passage, despite Republican control of the chamber, indicates that some lawmakers prioritize constitutional checks and balances over partisan loyalty on this particular issue.

cards.headline: Trump administration pushes to expand AI use in American medical care
cards.teaser: A White House backed effort aims to bring artificial intelligence tools into clinical practice despite provider concerns.
cards.body:
The Trump administration is supporting initiatives to introduce AI powered diagnostic and treatment tools into American medicine. The push comes as AI adoption surges across the healthcare sector, though medical providers have raised concerns about potential deskilling of clinical staff. Some doctors have warned that relying on AI in healthcare represents a significant risk.

Healthcare organizations are exploring what they call agentic AI to drive business value in medical enterprises. Proponents argue the technology can improve efficiency and outcomes when used appropriately. The debate over AI in medicine centers on balancing technological capabilities with the need to maintain human clinical judgment and expertise.

cards.headline: Marjane Satrapi, Author of Persepolis, Dies at 56
cards.teaser: The graphic novelist whose work chronicled the Islamic revolution in Iran has died.
cards.body:
Marjane Satrapi, the Iranian-French author and illustrator known for her graphic novel series Persepolis, has died at age 56. The autobiographical work, published in English in 2003, chronicled an Iranian girl's life through the Islamic revolution and the Iran-Iraq War.

Satrapi's graphic novels reached millions of readers worldwide and became a staple in schools and universities. Her visual storytelling enabled Western audiences to connect with and understand Iranian experiences during a transformative period in the nation's history.

cards.headline: Ukraine Accused of Strikes That Killed Four in Russian-Occupied Crimea
cards.teaser: Russian-backed officials say attacks in the occupied peninsula left at least 10 people injured.
cards.body:
Original Card Text Returned

At least four people were killed in attacks in Russian-occupied Crimea that officials blame on Ukraine, according to Russian-backed authorities in the region. At least 10 people were injured in the strikes.

The attacks represent the latest violence in the peninsula, which Russia seized from Ukraine in 2014. Ukrainian forces have increasingly targeted Russian military installations and infrastructure in Crimea as part of their broader military campaign.

cards.headline: Missing Sherpa Guide Found Alive on Mount Everest After Six Days
cards.teaser: Dawa Sherpa was discovered crawling toward Base Camp after disappearing at higher altitude.
cards.body:
Cleaners working on Mount Everest discovered Dawa Sherpa crawling toward Base Camp six days after he went missing at higher altitude. The find has been described as a "miracle" self-rescue, given the extreme conditions on the mountain.

Survival for multiple days at high altitude without shelter or supplies is exceptionally rare, making Sherpa's discovery a remarkable outcome.

cards.headline: Gunfire Erupts in Somali Capital as Election Dispute Escalates
cards.teaser: Opposition groups called for protests after the president's term was extended by a year.
cards.body:
Heavy gunfire erupted in Mogadishu as political tensions escalated over the president's decision to extend his term by one year. Opposition groups have organized street protests against the extension, contending that it violates democratic principles.

The violence underscores Somalia's broader security instability. The government continues to face challenges maintaining control over territory claimed by militant groups operating within the country.

cards.headline: Bondi Beach Shooting Hero Charged With Domestic Assault
cards.teaser: Ahmed al Ahmed disarmed one of the attackers during a deadly assault at a Jewish event.
cards.body:
Ahmed al-Ahmed, the 44-year-old Sydney man credited with disarming one of the gunmen during the Bondi terror attack in December, has been charged with assaulting his father. Police allege that al-Ahmed put his father in a headlock during an incident on 9 March at a house in Bankstown, in Sydney's west.

The domestic assault charges are separate from the shooting incident where al-Ahmed's actions were praised for preventing further casualties.

cards.headline: China Warns Families Not to Visit Tiananmen Victims' Graves on 37th Anniversary
cards.teaser: Police told relatives of those killed in the 1989 crackdown to stay away from cemeteries.
cards.body:
Chinese police warned families of those killed in the 1989 Tiananmen Square crackdown not to visit graves on the 37th anniversary of the military assault. The directive represents the latest effort by authorities to suppress public remembrance of the event.

The Tiananmen crackdown occurred when the Chinese military moved against pro-democracy protesters in Beijing, killing hundreds or possibly thousands of people. The Chinese government continues to censor discussion of the event and restricts commemoration activities.

hero.headline: National Guard deployment in Washington shows no effect on violent crime, study finds
hero.body:
A new study has found that the National Guard's presence in Washington, D.C. has had no measurable impact on reducing violent crime in the city. The Guard has been deployed since August as part of a federal task force aimed at addressing crime, and their numbers are scheduled to double in the coming weeks.

The deployment represents a significant federal intervention in local public safety operations, with Guard members working alongside the Metropolitan Police Department. As of recently, nearly 2,400 National Guard troops are stationed in Washington, with the operation costing approximately one million dollars daily.

The Guard's presence in the capital was extended through at least February by Pete Hegseth, the Defense Secretary, after the initial order was set to expire in November. This extension comes as the Trump administration has expanded its use of federal law enforcement to address crime in major cities.

The deployment has already drawn legal challenges. The District of Columbia's attorney general, Brian Schwalb, sued the Trump administration over the Guard's presence, characterizing it as an "involuntary military occupation" and an illegal use of the military for domestic law enforcement purposes. A federal judge previously ruled that Trump's deployment of National Guard troops to Los Angeles following immigration-related protests in June had been illegal, though that ruling does not directly apply to Washington, where the president has greater control over Guard operations.

The study's findings come as the administration has escalated its use of federal forces in American cities. Beyond Washington, Guard troops have been sent to Chicago, and officials have threatened deployments to Democratic-led cities including San Francisco, Portland and New York.

The Pentagon has moved to formalize these operations. In October, a top military official ordered National Guard units in all 50 states, the District of Columbia and U.S. territories to establish "quick reaction forces" trained in riot control tactics, including the use of batons, body shields, Tasers and pepper spray. According to an internal Pentagon directive, most states are required to train 500 National Guard members in these tactics, amounting to roughly 23,500 troops nationwide. States are required to report monthly on their progress.

Despite the study's conclusions about ineffectiveness, federal officials have not commented on the findings or indicated whether they will reconsider the strategy. The planned expansion of Guard personnel is proceeding as scheduled.

The deployment raises questions about resource allocation and the appropriate role of military forces in addressing urban crime. As Washington continues to grapple with public safety concerns, residents and policymakers are watching to see whether the expanded Guard presence will produce different results or whether alternative approaches to crime reduction will need to be considered.

cards.headline: California governor's race remains undecided as vote counting continues
cards.teaser: Vote counting continues in California's gubernatorial primary with several candidates locked in tight races.
cards.body:
California's governor's race remains unsettled as state election officials continue sorting through uncounted primary ballots, a process that could take days or weeks to complete.

According to polls, conservative pundit Steve Hilton was narrowly leading the race, with former US health and human services secretary Xavier Becerra in second place. Billionaire Tom Steyer trailed behind both candidates. Under California's primary system, the top two vote-getters will advance to the general election.

cards.headline: Obama Presidential Center opens later this month in Chicago
cards.teaser: The $850 million Obama Presidential Center will open to the public in Chicago later this month.
cards.body:
The Obama Presidential Center is opening later this month in Chicago as a major new addition to the nation's presidential libraries and museums. The $850 million facility features distinctive architecture that has drawn considerable attention.

The center will showcase exhibits and materials from Barack Obama's presidency while serving as a community resource. It will provide educational programs and public spaces for visitors to engage with presidential history.

cards.headline: More than one-third of World Cup matches face dangerous heat conditions
cards.teaser: An analysis finds that dangerously hot and humid weather is likely at many 2026 World Cup venues.
cards.body:
More than one-third of matches at the 2026 World Cup are expected to face dangerously hot and humid weather conditions, according to an NPR analysis. Researchers examined typical weather patterns at tournament venues and the scheduled timing of games to identify which matches carry the highest heat risk.

The findings highlight concerns about player safety and competitive fairness during the competition. Multiple venues scheduled to host matches are located in areas where dangerous heat and humidity are likely to occur during the tournament period.

cards.headline: Primary elections take shape across multiple states
cards.teaser: Primary elections in California, Iowa, New Jersey and other states have set up midterm election matchups.
cards.body:
Primary elections held across California, Iowa, New Jersey and three other states have determined matchups for upcoming midterm elections. The results shape the political landscape heading into general election contests.

The primaries have answered some questions about candidate selection while leaving others unresolved. Voters in multiple states cast ballots to select party nominees who will compete in midterm races later this year.

cards.headline: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle celebrate daughter Lilibet's fifth birthday
cards.teaser: The Duke and Duchess of Sussex shared a photo of their daughter Lilibet on her fifth birthday.
cards.body:
Prince Harry and Meghan Markle marked their daughter Lilibet's fifth birthday by releasing a photograph of her. In the accompanying message, the Duke and Duchess of Sussex referred to her affectionately as their "dream girl."

The couple, who stepped away from their royal responsibilities and relocated to the United States, periodically share glimpses of their family. Lilibet is their second child.

cards.headline: UK teenager sentenced to life for knife murder committed while on bail
cards.teaser: A 17-year-old will serve a minimum of 17 years for killing John McNab in an unprovoked attack.
cards.body:
A 17-year-old has been sentenced to life imprisonment for stabbing John McNab, 22, to death in Leith last year. The attack was unprovoked, and the teenager will serve a minimum of 17 years before becoming eligible for parole.

The case has raised concerns about bail procedures, as the offender was on bail for a previous slashing offense at the time of the murder.

hero.headline: SpaceX sets IPO price at $135 per share, targeting largest stock market debut
hero.body:
SpaceX has set a target share price of $135 for its initial public offering, positioning the space exploration company for what would be the largest stock market debut in history. The pricing values the company at $1.75 trillion ahead of its planned debut on the Nasdaq next week. The company announced the pricing earlier than market observers expected.

The IPO structure allows investors to purchase shares in Elon Musk's privately held space company for the first time. At the $1.75 trillion valuation, SpaceX would rank among the most valuable publicly traded companies globally from its first day of trading. The share price and timing suggest strong demand for access to the commercial space sector.

The public offering could significantly increase Musk's personal wealth, with analysts suggesting the listing might make him the world's first trillionaire. Musk currently holds the title of world's richest person through his stakes in SpaceX, Tesla, and X. The SpaceX valuation would add substantially to his existing net worth.

Investment interest in the offering has been intense, with traders moving into related mid-cap stocks in anticipation of the debut. The company has built its value through contracts with NASA, commercial satellite launches, and its Starlink internet service. SpaceX has established itself as the dominant player in commercial space launches over the past decade.

The IPO represents a shift for SpaceX, which has operated as a private company since its founding. The decision to go public provides the company with access to public capital markets for future expansion while allowing early investors and employees to realize gains on their holdings. Market observers will watch closely to see if the debut meets the ambitious valuation target when trading begins next week.

cards.headline: S&P 500 futures drop as Broadcom earnings miss drags down chip stocks
cards.teaser: Stock index futures fell after Broadcom led semiconductor stocks lower in premarket trading.
cards.body:
S&P 500 futures declined following Broadcom's disappointing earnings results. The weakness spread across the semiconductor sector, with Micron, Marvell, and Broadcom all posting significant premarket losses. Nasdaq futures fell while Dow futures gained, reflecting divergent market moves.

The chip sector's retreat disrupted momentum in artificial intelligence-related stocks. Emerging market equities also weakened as investors reassessed the outlook for AI investment spending.

cards.headline: TSMC says chip supply will not meet AI demand for years
cards.teaser: The world's largest contract chipmaker warned that production capacity will lag behind artificial intelligence fueled demand.
cards.body:
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company's CEO warned that semiconductor supply will struggle to keep pace with artificial intelligence-driven demand for years ahead. TSMC remains the world's leading producer of advanced chips for AI systems.

The company's leadership expressed confidence in its competitive position, even as it faces growing competition from Chinese chipmakers. The supply shortage underscores the difficulty of scaling production fast enough to match surging demand for AI computing power.

cards.headline: Bill Ackman's Pershing Square exits Universal Music stake with $600 million profit
cards.teaser: The hedge fund is selling its position in the music company after Universal rejected a takeover bid.
cards.body:
Pershing Square has sold its stake in Universal Music Group, realizing a $600 million profit on the investment. The exit comes after Bill Ackman's hedge fund made an unsuccessful acquisition proposal for the music giant. Universal Music's share price fell 7 percent following the announcement of both the stake sale and the failed takeover bid.

The decision allows Pershing Square to capitalize on its investment gains without securing a full acquisition of one of the world's largest music companies.

cards.headline: Trump administration pushes to expand AI use in American medical care
cards.teaser: A White House backed effort aims to bring artificial intelligence tools into clinical practice despite provider concerns.
cards.body:
The Trump administration is supporting initiatives to introduce AI powered diagnostic and treatment tools into American medicine. The push comes as AI adoption surges across the healthcare sector, though medical providers have raised concerns about potential deskilling of clinical staff. Some doctors have warned that relying on AI in healthcare represents a significant risk.

Healthcare organizations are exploring what they call agentic AI to drive business value in medical enterprises. Proponents argue the technology can improve efficiency and outcomes when used appropriately. The debate over AI in medicine centers on balancing technological capabilities with the need to maintain human clinical judgment and expertise.

cards.headline: Asian markets fall as semiconductor rally cools and tensions rise
cards.teaser: Stock indexes across Asia dropped as chip stocks retreated and Middle East fighting undermined a ceasefire.
cards.body:
Asian stock markets declined as the recent rally in semiconductor stocks lost momentum and renewed fighting in the Middle East raised concerns. Asia Pacific markets fell on tensions between the United States and Iran, despite an earlier ceasefire agreement. Oil prices eased from recent highs but remained elevated.

European shares climbed while Asian shares retreated after US stocks paused their record breaking rally. The mixed global performance reflected uncertainty about the sustainability of recent gains and geopolitical risks. Investors shifted focus from technology sector momentum to broader economic and security concerns affecting multiple regions.

cards.headline: Small business owners deploy AI agents to handle operations
cards.teaser: Entrepreneurs are turning artificial intelligence systems loose on finances, email, and customer service.
cards.body:
Small business owners are increasingly using AI agents to manage core business functions including financial operations, email communications, and customer interactions. The technology allows entrepreneurs to scale operations without adding human staff, creating what some describe as armies of AI employees. The systems can work continuously across multiple business tasks.

The shift raises questions about reliability and control when critical business functions are automated. Business owners must weigh the efficiency gains against potential risks of delegating decision making to AI systems. The trend reflects broader adoption of artificial intelligence tools in small and medium sized enterprises seeking competitive advantages.

hero.headline: Flesh-eating screwworm detected in South Texas for first time in decades
hero.body:
The United States Department of Agriculture has confirmed the presence of New World screwworm in South Texas, marking a significant breakthrough in the parasite's containment. The detection comes after decades of successful efforts to keep the flesh-eating insect south of the US-Mexico border.

The New World screwworm is a parasitic fly whose larvae burrow into wounds on warm-blooded animals, including humans and livestock. Once inside, the larvae feed on living tissue using sharp mouths to create severe infections that can be fatal if untreated. Female flies lay eggs in any open wound, and hundreds of larvae can emerge from a single infestation.

For much of the 20th century, screwworm infestations devastated the American livestock industry. In the 1950s, scientists developed an elegant solution using radiation to sterilize fly eggs. Because female flies typically mate only once, encounters with sterile males meant eggs would not fertilize, and populations began declining. This sterile-fly program proved so successful that it gradually pushed the screwworm southward, eventually establishing a containment zone at the Darién Gap between Panama and South America.

However, the parasite has been creeping northward again in recent years, probably assisted by cross-border livestock trade. About 89,000 cases have been detected in animals across Central America over the past three years, according to FDA chief Marty Makary. The screwworm now sits only a few hundred miles south of the United States border.

Recent budget cuts to scientific research and international aid programs have complicated containment efforts. Some global screwworm-fighting initiatives were reduced during the Trump administration, shaking international cooperation that had been crucial to the program's decades of success. Yet in response to rising case numbers, the USDA announced in June that it would reopen a Texas breeding facility for sterile flies, followed by an ambitious $850 million plan in August to combat the screwworm.

A Maryland resident diagnosed with screwworm in August after traveling to El Salvador provided a warning signal. Medical experts emphasized that human transmission risk remains very low, as the infection was caught before the insect could mature. However, the case highlighted how closely the parasite has approached US territory and underscored the importance of international cooperation on research and prevention.

The USDA and Texas animal health officials are expanding monitoring programs to trap flies and continuing inspections of livestock headed for slaughter. Officials worry that wildlife could also carry the parasite across the border, citing a 2016 infestation among Florida Keys deer that required releasing sterile flies to control.

Experts stress the real threat involves livestock populations, particularly in Texas with its large cattle industry. Timothy Schell, acting director of the Center for Veterinary Medicine at the FDA, warned that screwworm could cause serious economic damage to American livestock production if it becomes established.

cards.headline: NASA ends MAVEN Mars mission after spacecraft spins out of control
cards.teaser: NASA declared the end of its MAVEN Mars orbiter mission after the spacecraft entered an unrecoverable state.
cards.body:
NASA has ended its MAVEN mission after the Mars orbiter entered an unrecoverable state following an orbital anomaly. The spacecraft, which had been spinning out of control behind Mars, is now officially declared dead.

MAVEN had exceeded its original mission timeline while studying the Martian atmosphere and climate. The orbiter provided significant scientific data about Mars's atmospheric evolution before the mission concluded.

cards.headline: Nvidia launches laptop chips to bring artificial intelligence to personal computers
cards.teaser: Nvidia introduced new processors designed to run artificial intelligence directly on laptops, expanding beyond data center hardware.
cards.body:
Nvidia announced a new line of chips aimed at bringing artificial intelligence capabilities from cloud data centers to personal computers. The company, working with Microsoft, unveiled the RTX Spark processor designed to enable what executives call personal AI on Windows laptops.

CEO Jensen Huang said the new chip will reinvent the PC by allowing users to run advanced AI models locally on their machines rather than relying on remote servers. The move represents Nvidia's effort to compete across every layer of the AI technology stack, from massive data center operations down to consumer devices.

cards.headline: Google releases Gemma 4 model that runs on laptops with 16GB of memory
cards.teaser: Google introduced Gemma 4 12B, a multimodal AI model small enough to operate on standard laptops without cloud connection.
cards.body:
Google launched its AI Edge Gallery on macOS, allowing Mac users to run Gemini language models locally on their computers. The company released Gemma 4 12B, a unified encoder-free multimodal model that can operate on any laptop with just 16GB of RAM.

Google DeepMind designed the model to enable local, agentic workflows without requiring massive computing resources or cloud connectivity. The company published specifications and guidelines for the technology, making it accessible to developers working on laptop-based AI applications.

cards.headline: Waymo repurposes used robotaxi batteries for power grid storage
cards.teaser: Waymo's retired autonomous vehicle batteries will provide backup energy storage for electrical grids in California and Texas.
cards.body:
Waymo announced that batteries removed from its self-driving taxi fleet will get second lives as stationary energy storage systems for power grids. The used batteries will support energy storage projects in California and Texas, helping to stabilize electricity supply.

The initiative represents a growing trend of repurposed electric vehicle batteries serving as grid-scale storage after they no longer meet the performance standards required for transportation. Battery packs that retain 70 to 80 percent of their original capacity can still provide years of useful service in less demanding stationary applications.

cards.headline: Nintendo confirms Switch 2 model with replaceable battery for European market
cards.teaser: Nintendo said it is developing a version of the Switch 2 with user-replaceable batteries specifically for sale in the European Union.
cards.body:
Nintendo officially confirmed it will sell Switch 2 models with user-replaceable batteries in the European Union to comply with new EU regulations taking effect February 18th, 2027. The company states it is "implementing measures to comply with these requirements" on its website.

The EU-specific model will allow users to easily replace the battery themselves, marking a significant upgrade from the current Switch design, which requires professional service for battery replacement.

cards.headline: Google publishes Fitbit Air blueprints for third-party accessory makers
cards.teaser: Google released CAD drawings and technical specifications for its Fitbit Air, inviting manufacturers to create custom bands and accessories.
cards.body:
Google has released the technical specifications and CAD drawings for the Fitbit Air fitness tracker to enable third-party accessory creation. The move opens the door for manufacturers and hobbyists to design compatible bands, cases, and other add-ons, including bicep band options.

This decision represents a shift in Google's approach to its wearable devices, allowing broader customization of the Fitbit Air beyond what the company itself produces.

hero.headline: Russell Wilson retires from NFL at 37, joins CBS Sports
hero.body:
Russell Wilson announced his retirement from professional football at age 37, ending a 13-year NFL career that included a Super Bowl championship and ten Pro Bowl selections. The veteran quarterback will transition to a broadcasting role with CBS Sports.

Wilson led the Seattle Seahawks to their first Super Bowl victory in 2014, defeating the Denver Broncos. Over his career, he established himself as one of the most successful quarterbacks of his generation, earning Pro Bowl honors ten times. His playing career included stints with the Seahawks, Broncos, and most recently another team before his retirement announcement.

The quarterback posted a video message titled "thank you, football" as he confirmed the career change to broadcasting. CBS Sports will add Wilson to its NFL coverage team, though specific details about his role have not been disclosed. The network gains a recently retired player with extensive playoff experience and deep knowledge of the modern game.

Wilson's retirement creates an immediate impact for his most recent team. Aaron Glenn, speaking about the quarterback situation, acknowledged Wilson's new television position and indicated his organization is evaluating options at the quarterback position. The timing of Wilson's announcement, coming during the offseason, allows teams to adjust their rosters and draft strategies accordingly.

The move from playing to broadcasting represents a growing trend of recently retired NFL players moving directly into media roles. Wilson's decade-plus of starting experience and championship pedigree position him as a potentially valuable analyst for CBS's NFL programming. His retirement removes one of the league's most recognizable veteran quarterbacks from active competition.

cards.headline: Knicks win NBA Finals opener over Spurs with late comeback
cards.teaser: New York overcame a 14-point third-quarter deficit to defeat San Antonio in Game 1 of the championship series.
cards.body:
The New York Knicks defeated the San Antonio Spurs 105-95 in Game 1 of the NBA Finals, overcoming a 14-point third-quarter deficit on the road. Knicks guard Jalen Brunson led the way with 30 points as New York kept Spurs star Victor Wembanyama quiet for stretches of the game.

The victory extends the Knicks' impressive playoff run to 11 consecutive wins and gives them a 1-0 series lead. New York is now three wins away from capturing their first championship since 1973.

cards.headline: Former Ireland and Lions rugby player Fergus Slattery dies at 77
cards.teaser: Blackrock College announced the death of the former back row who represented Ireland and the British and Irish Lions.
cards.body:
Fergus Slattery, the former Ireland and British and Irish Lions back row, has died at the age of 77. Blackrock College announced his passing.

Slattery was a notable figure in Irish rugby during his playing career, representing his country and the Lions during his international years.

cards.headline: FIFA bans reusable water bottles at World Cup stadiums
cards.teaser: The late policy change citing safety concerns has drawn criticism from heat experts who warn of health risks.
cards.body:
FIFA has prohibited fans from bringing reusable water bottles into World Cup stadiums, reversing an earlier policy that allowed empty, transparent plastic bottles. The governing body cited safety concerns, stating the ban prevents the risk of injury if bottles are thrown at players or attendees. Other containers including cups, jars, and cans are also prohibited under the updated stadium code of conduct.

The last-minute policy change has drawn concern from spectators worried about access to drinking water during matches, particularly given heat conditions at the tournament venues.

cards.headline: Manchester City considers legal action after Real Madrid candidate promises Haaland signing
cards.teaser: A presidential election candidate unveiled an Erling Haaland shirt on live television during the Real Madrid campaign.
cards.body:
Manchester City is considering legal action against Enrique Riquelme, a candidate in Real Madrid's presidential election, after he displayed a Madrid shirt bearing Erling Haaland's name on live television. Riquelme claimed that a clause in Haaland's contract would enable him to sign the striker if elected to lead Real Madrid.

The club has dismissed suggestions that Haaland will leave for Spain. Riquelme also claimed that midfielder Rodri wanted to join Real Madrid, the record 15-times European Champions League winners. Haaland recently signed a nine-and-a-half-year contract extension with City in January 2025.

cards.headline: U.S. Women's Open begins at Riviera Country Club with 156-player field
cards.teaser: World number one Nelly Korda leads the field at the tournament in Los Angeles.
cards.body:
The U.S. Women's Open tees off at Riviera Country Club with 156 players competing for the championship. The tournament field includes world number one Nelly Korda and former champion Michelle Wie West.

Korda stated she feels more comfortable heading into this year's championship. The tournament at Riviera represents a significant event on the LPGA calendar, drawing top players from around the world to the Los Angeles venue.

cards.headline: England's Emilio Gay out for eight on Test debut against New Zealand
cards.teaser: The batsman was caught off Kyle Jamieson's bowling as England reached 16-1 at Lord's.
cards.body:
Emilio Gay's Test debut ended in disappointment as he was caught off Kyle Jamieson's bowling for eight runs on the first morning of England's match against New Zealand at Lord's. The dismissal came with England's score at 16-1 during the opening session.

Gay had shown some promise earlier in the innings when he guided a full toss from Jamieson away behind square, but he could not build on that start against the New Zealand attack.

hero.headline: Marjane Satrapi, creator of Persepolis, dies at 56
hero.body:
Marjane Satrapi, the French-Iranian artist and filmmaker known for her autobiographical graphic novel and animated film Persepolis, has died at age 56. A statement from close friends and family said Satrapi died of sadness a little over a year after the death of her husband, Mattias Ripa.

Satrapi became internationally recognized for Persepolis, which chronicled her childhood in Iran during the Islamic Revolution and her adolescence in Europe. The graphic novel series was adapted into an animated feature film in 2007, which she co-directed. The film received an Oscar nomination and won the Jury Prize at the Cannes Film Festival.

Born in Iran, Satrapi left the country as a teenager and eventually settled in France, where she built her career as an artist, author, and filmmaker. Her work combined stark black-and-white illustrations with personal storytelling that addressed political upheaval, cultural identity, and displacement. Persepolis was published in multiple languages and became widely used in schools and universities.

Beyond Persepolis, Satrapi directed live-action films and continued to create graphic novels. Her work as an animator and director expanded her influence in both literature and cinema, making her one of the most prominent voices bridging the two mediums.

Satrapi's death follows the loss of her husband, whom friends and family described as the love of her life. She leaves behind a body of work that shaped how graphic novels are perceived as a serious literary and cinematic form.

cards.headline: Bayeux Tapestry to travel to London with careful safeguards
cards.teaser: French officials say the 950-year-old Bayeux Tapestry will be protected during its planned move to London.
cards.body:
The Bayeux Tapestry, an 11th-century embroidery depicting the Norman conquest of England, will travel to London in a carefully planned operation across the Channel. French Culture Minister Catherine Pégard emphasized that "nothing has been left to chance" in preparing for this historic loan.

The fragile artifact will be transported in a specially constructed cradle housed within a protective container, designed to eliminate jolts, bumps, shakes, and vibrations during the journey. The meticulous preparations underscore the importance of safeguarding this 950-year-old work as it makes its rare voyage from France.

cards.headline: Cannes Film Festival director reflects on 2026 edition
cards.teaser: Thierry Fremaux discussed the 79th Cannes Film Festival, which concluded with fewer Hollywood blockbusters but strong competition.
cards.body:
The 79th Cannes Film Festival wrapped with familiar complaints about fewer Hollywood blockbusters and American stars. The competition lineup delivered a series of beloved films but no immediate consensus masterpiece.

Thierry Fremaux, the festival director, offered a different perspective. He said Cannes has never been more competitive, more influential, or more important, despite the shift in Hollywood participation and industry restructuring.

cards.headline: Harry and Meghan release photo for daughter Lilibet's fifth birthday
cards.teaser: The Duke and Duchess of Sussex shared a picture of their daughter Lilibet, calling her their dream girl.
cards.body:
Prince Harry and Meghan Markle shared a photograph of their daughter Lilibet to celebrate her fifth birthday. In an accompanying statement, the couple referred to her as "our dream girl."

The Duke and Duchess of Sussex have periodically released images of their children to the public. Lilibet is their second child.

cards.headline: Neon executive discusses recent Cannes win and film distribution
cards.teaser: Tom Quinn of Neon spoke about the distributor's seventh consecutive Palme d'Or win at Cannes.
cards.body:
Tom Quinn, an executive at independent distributor Neon, spoke at SXSW London shortly after the company secured its seventh consecutive Palme d'Or at Cannes for Cristian Mungiu's film Fjord. Quinn praised Neon's recent wins as an "obsession," emphasizing his view of the company's projects as cinema rather than content for other platforms.

Neon has emerged as a significant force in independent film distribution since its founding. The company is approaching its tenth anniversary while maintaining an impressive track record at major film festivals and establishing itself as a major player in the industry.

cards.headline: Universal Music Greater China signs Jason Zhang in major deal
cards.teaser: One of the most commercially successful Chinese-language pop artists has joined Universal Music in a wide-ranging partnership.
cards.body:
Universal Music Greater China has signed Jason Zhang, a leading figure in Chinese-language pop music, under a comprehensive agreement. The deal covers recorded music, artist management, live performance, and international strategy, and was structured in partnership with Zhang's own label, Planet Culture.

In a related move, Universal Music Group announced a strategic investment in Solution One, a Thai music distributor, as part of its broader expansion in the Asia-Pacific region.

cards.headline: Ted Danson says he will apologize for blackface roast of Whoopi Goldberg
cards.teaser: The actor addressed a 1993 incident in which he performed in blackface at a roast of Whoopi Goldberg.
cards.body:
Ted Danson said he will apologize for the rest of my life for performing in blackface at a roast of Whoopi Goldberg in 1993. Speaking on W. Kamau Bell's podcast, the actor called the incident arrogant and stupid.

The roast took place at the New York Friars Club while Danson was starring in Cheers. He later appeared in The Good Place and other television projects.

hero.headline: Four House Republicans vote against Trump on Iran resolution
hero.teaser: A House resolution on Iran revealed growing impatience with Trump's military policy, even within his own party.
hero.body:
The House of Representatives delivered a significant rebuke to President Trump on Wednesday by voting 215 to 208 in favor of a war powers resolution that would force him to seek congressional approval before continuing military operations against Iran or withdraw U.S. forces from the conflict.

Four Republicans joined all Democrats to support the measure. The dissident Republicans were Thomas Massie of Kentucky, Brian Fitzpatrick of Pennsylvania, Warren Davidson of Ohio, and Tom Barrett of Michigan.

The vote represents a notable moment of Republican defection on a key foreign policy issue. It demonstrates that some members of Trump's own party are willing to challenge his approach to military conflict, despite the president's significant influence over the GOP.

The resolution now moves to the Senate, where lawmakers must promptly take up the measure under the war powers law. A handful of Senate Republicans previously joined Democrats in advancing a similar resolution last month, indicating potential support in the upper chamber as well.

This marks the fourth time the House has voted on a resolution designed to limit Trump's authority to continue the Iran conflict, which has now lasted more than 90 days. House Republicans had previously cancelled an earlier scheduled vote, recognizing they lacked sufficient numbers to block the measure's passage.

The timing of the vote comes as diplomatic efforts to negotiate a settlement have stalled. Trump administration officials have repeatedly claimed that a deal is close and that Iran is eager to reach an agreement, but concrete progress remains elusive.

The war powers resolution is largely symbolic in nature, as significant procedural hurdles remain before Congress could actually compel the president to end military operations. The measure would require Senate passage and potentially a presidential veto override to become binding policy. Still, the House vote signals growing frustration among lawmakers across the aisle regarding the administration's handling of the conflict.

The four Republican defectors represent a minority within their party, but their willingness to break ranks highlights the genuine concerns some GOP members hold about executive power in military matters. Historically, questions about the balance between presidential authority and congressional oversight in military conflicts have periodically united lawmakers across party lines.

The vote reflects evolving dynamics within Congress as members grapple with the ongoing tension between supporting a president of their own party and asserting institutional congressional powers over matters of war and peace. The resolution's passage, despite Republican control of the chamber, indicates that some lawmakers prioritize constitutional checks and balances over partisan loyalty on this particular issue.

cards.headline: Trump to nominate Todd Blanche as attorney general
cards.teaser: President Trump announced he will formally nominate acting Attorney General Todd Blanche to lead the Justice Department.
cards.body:
President Trump will formally nominate acting Attorney General Todd Blanche to serve as the nation's top prosecutor. Trump announced the decision Wednesday evening, with nomination paperwork expected Thursday. Blanche previously worked as Trump's personal criminal defense attorney before being appointed to lead the Justice Department in an acting capacity.

If confirmed by the Senate, Blanche would become the administration's permanent attorney general. The Senate confirmation process will allow lawmakers to examine his record and qualifications for the role.

cards.headline: Defeated Republican incumbents signal independence from Trump agenda
cards.teaser: GOP lawmakers who did not receive Trump's backing in the midterms are taking a more independent stance on his legislative priorities.
cards.body:
Republican incumbents who were passed over for Trump's endorsement during the midterm elections are increasingly willing to challenge the president's agenda. The shift creates new complications for GOP leadership as they work to advance key legislation in the coming weeks.

Republican leaders are attempting to pass an immigration enforcement funding package and secure other legislative wins. The willingness of some members to buck Trump's priorities could complicate efforts to maintain party unity on major votes.

cards.headline: Deb Haaland wins Democratic primary for New Mexico governor
cards.teaser: The former Biden administration official could become the first female Native American governor if elected in the general election.
cards.body:
Deb Haaland secured the Democratic nomination for governor of New Mexico in the state's primary election. Haaland previously served in the Biden administration before leaving to pursue the gubernatorial race.

If successful in the general election, Haaland would make history as the first female Native American to serve as a state governor. Her primary victory positions her as the Democratic candidate heading into the fall campaign.

cards.headline: Trump picks Bill Pulte to lead intelligence community
cards.teaser: The president tapped the current head of the Federal Housing Finance Agency to additionally serve as acting director of national intelligence.
cards.body:
President Trump announced Bill Pulte, who currently leads the Federal Housing Finance Agency, will serve as acting director of national intelligence without seeking Senate confirmation. The move has drawn criticism from lawmakers, including Republican Mitch McConnell, who suggested Pulte is unfit for the role.

The appointment is complicating efforts to renew warrantless surveillance powers in Congress. Lawmakers are expressing hesitation about extending these authorities given Trump's approach to filling senior intelligence positions without legislative approval, potentially jeopardizing the renewal process.

cards.headline: Marco Rubio says white South Africans assimilate more easily
cards.teaser: The secretary of state defended a new program for white South Africans by citing their ability to assimilate into American society.
cards.body:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio told lawmakers that white South Africans assimilate more easily when questioned about a new Trump administration program. The administration stopped admitting refugees and created a separate pathway specifically for white South Africans.

Rubio made the remarks during testimony before Congress this week. The program has drawn scrutiny for its focus on one demographic group from South Africa while broader refugee admissions remain suspended.

cards.headline: Katie Porter and Steve Hilton lead in California governor primary
cards.teaser: Early results show Democrat Xavier Becerra and Republican Steve Hilton advancing in the race to replace Governor Gavin Newsom.
cards.body:
Republican Steve Hilton is narrowly leading California's gubernatorial primary, with Democrat Xavier Becerra in second place. Under the state's top-two primary system, the leading vote-getters from each party will advance to the general election.

State election officials continue counting ballots in what could be a lengthy process spanning days or weeks. The race to replace Governor Gavin Newsom also features Democrat Tom Steyer, along with Republican Chad Bianco.
